metadata.title: RAC DA40 Checkride Trainer
metadata.disclaimer: Training aid only; AFM/POH and current controlled RAC SOP take precedence.

questions.prompt: According to the QRC, what is the speed for straight and level flight in Exercise 6?
questions.explanation: Exercise 6 step 3 states: 'Speed 110 KIAS (±65% power setting)'.

questions.prompt: What power setting does the QRC specify for straight and level flight at 110 KIAS?
questions.explanation: Exercise 6 step 3: 'Speed 110 KIAS (±65% power setting)'.

questions.prompt: Enter the QRC speed and power setting for straight and level flight (Exercise 6).
questions.explanation: Exercise 6 step 3: 'Speed 110 KIAS (±65% power setting)'.

questions.prompt: Put the initial steps for establishing straight and level flight (Exercise 6) in the correct order.
steps: Look out – select an outside reference point
Pitch for horizontal flight
Speed 110 KIAS (±65% power setting)
Trim as required
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
questions.explanation: These are steps 1–6 of 'Straight and level flight' in Exercise 6, in QRC order.

questions.prompt: Which item is included in the 'Look out and check' list for straight and level flight in the QRC?
questions.explanation: Exercise 6 step 7 lists: fuel quantity and fuel balance, radio, engine instruments, direction (outside reference point), altitude. The other options are take-off line-up items from Exercise 12, not the Exercise 6 check list.

questions.prompt: Enter the QRC climb speed and the power setting used when approaching that speed during the transition to climb.
questions.explanation: Exercise 7 'Transition to climb': step 3 'Pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)', step 4 'Approaching 80 KIAS, set full power (100%)'.

questions.prompt: During the transition to climb, when does the QRC say to set full power (100%)?
choices: Before pitching for the climb attitude
questions.explanation: Exercise 7 'Transition to climb' step 4: 'Approaching 80 KIAS, set full power (100%)'.

questions.prompt: How far before the target altitude does the QRC say to begin the level-off from a climb?
questions.explanation: Exercise 7 'Level-off from climb' step 1: '±20 ft before target altitude, set pitch for horizontal flight'. (±50 ft applies to level-off from descent for approach; ±100 ft to level-off from glide descent.)

questions.prompt: Put the steps of the transition to climb (Exercise 7) in the correct order.
steps: Look out – scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Check engine instruments
Pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)
Approaching 80 KIAS, set full power (100%)
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Trim as required
questions.explanation: These are steps 1–6 of 'Transition to climb (80 KIAS)' in Exercise 7, in QRC order.

questions.prompt: During the level-off from a climb, what power is set when approaching 110 KIAS?
questions.explanation: Exercise 7 'Level-off from climb (110 KIAS)' step 4: 'Approaching 110 KIAS, ±65% power'.

questions.prompt: Enter the QRC values for the transition to cruise descent: power setting, standard descent rate, and speed.
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 'Transition to cruise descent': step 1 'Reduce power to ±20% (standard descent 500 ft/min)', step 2 'Pitch to maintain 110 KIAS'.

questions.prompt: For the level-off from a cruise descent, the QRC says to increase power to ±65% how far before the target altitude?
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 'Level-off from cruise descent' step 1: '±20 ft before the target altitude, increase power to ±65%'.

questions.prompt: What is the target speed for the descent for approach, and to what power is the lever reduced during the transition?
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 'Transition to descent for approach (90 KIAS)': step 2 'Power – smoothly reduce power lever to ±20%', step 3 decelerate to 90 KIAS and set pitch attitude to capture the descent.

questions.prompt: For the level-off from a descent for approach, enter how far before the target altitude the level-off begins and the level flight power setting.
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 'Level-off from descent for approach (90 KIAS)' step 1: '±50 ft before target altitude, smoothly increase power to level flight setting (±45%)'.

questions.prompt: What power and speed does the QRC specify for the glide descent?
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 'Transition to glide descent (75 KIAS)': step 3 'Power idle', step 4 'Set pitch for gliding flight (75 KIAS)'.

questions.prompt: How far before the target altitude does the QRC say to begin the level-off from a glide descent?
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 'Level-off from glide descent' step 1: '±100 ft before the target altitude, increase power to increase speed to 110 KIAS (±65% power)'.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of the transition to glide descent (Exercise 8) in the correct order.
steps: Look out – select an outside reference point
Check engine instruments
Power idle
Set pitch for gliding flight (75 KIAS)
Trim as required
Maintain wings level using ailerons
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
questions.explanation: These are steps 1–7 of 'Transition to glide descent (75 KIAS)' in Exercise 8, in QRC order.

questions.prompt: What bank angle does the QRC specify for a normal coordinated turn?
questions.explanation: Exercise 9 'Normal coordinated turn (30° bank)' step 2: 'Roll into 30° bank, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw'. (45° is the steep turn in Exercise 15; 20° is the climbing turn maximum.)

questions.prompt: What is the maximum bank angle permitted in a climbing turn according to the QRC?
questions.explanation: Exercise 9 'Climbing turn' step 3: 'Max. bank 20°, use rudder to counteract adverse yaw'.

questions.prompt: Enter the bank angle and power setting the QRC specifies for a descending turn (cruise descent established per Chapter 8).
questions.explanation: Exercise 9 'Descending turn': step 2 'Establish cruise descent (as explained in Chapter 8, power ±25%)', step 3 'Bank 30°'.

questions.prompt: According to the QRC, why is rudder used when rolling into and out of a turn?
choices: To keep the nose on the horizon
To control the rate of descent
questions.explanation: Exercise 9 states for the normal coordinated turn, climbing turn and descending turn: 'use rudder to counteract adverse yaw'.

questions.prompt: Per the QRC, how is a descending turn established before banking into the turn?
choices: Establish a normal climb (as explained in Exercise 7)
Establish a cruise descent (as explained in Chapter 8, power ±25%)
Set power idle and pitch for gliding flight (75 KIAS)
Set power ±45% and decelerate to 90 KIAS
questions.explanation: Exercise 9 'Descending turn' step 2: 'Establish cruise descent (as explained in Chapter 8, power ±25%)'.

questions.prompt: Put the steps to decelerate from 110 to 60 KIAS (flaps T/O) in the correct order.
steps: Look out – scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Set power ±20%
Flaps T/O below 108 KIAS, adjust pitch
Maintain altitude / direction
Speed approaches 60 KIAS, set power ±35%
Trim
questions.explanation: These are steps 1–6 of 'Decelerate from 110 to 60 KIAS (flaps T/O)' in Exercise 10A, in QRC order.

questions.prompt: Below what speed does the QRC say to select flaps T/O when decelerating from 110 to 60 KIAS?
questions.explanation: Exercise 10A 'Decelerate from 110 to 60 KIAS (flaps T/O)' step 3: 'flaps T/O below 108 KIAS, adjust pitch'.

questions.prompt: When decelerating from 110 to 60 KIAS (flaps T/O), enter the power set at the start and the power set as the speed approaches 60 KIAS.
questions.explanation: Exercise 10A step 2 'Set power ±20%' and step 5 'Speed approaches 60 KIAS, set power ±35%'.

questions.prompt: When accelerating from 60 to 110 KIAS (flaps T/O), at what speed does the QRC say to select flaps up?
questions.explanation: Exercise 10A 'Accelerate from 60 to 110 KIAS (flaps T/O)' step 2: 'Flaps up (speed ±70 KIAS), adjust pitch'.

questions.prompt: When decelerating from 110 to 65 KIAS with flaps up, what power is set approaching 65 KIAS?
questions.explanation: Exercise 10A 'Decelerate from 110 to 65 KIAS (flaps up)' step 4: 'Approaching 65 KIAS, Power ±35%'. (±20% is the initial setting in step 2.)

questions.prompt: When accelerating from 60 to 110 KIAS (flaps T/O), enter the power set at the start of the acceleration and the power set approaching 110 KIAS.
questions.explanation: Exercise 10A 'Accelerate from 60 to 110 KIAS (flaps T/O)': step 1 'Full power (100%)', step 4 'Approaching 110 KIAS, reduce power to ±65%'.

questions.prompt: According to the QRC, recovery from a FULL stall is started at which indication?
choices: Nose and/or wing drop, or an (excessive) rate of descent with full back pressure
Stall warning, buffet, or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first
Stall warning, buffet, or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the green arc, whichever comes first
The first buffet, followed by a second buffet to confirm
questions.explanation: The QRC 'Recovery of the stall is started at' table states that for a full stall recovery begins at nose and/or wing drop or (excessive) rate of descent with full back pressure. The other criteria belong to the approach to stall (landing and clean configurations).

questions.prompt: State the minimum altitudes by which a FULL stall must be recovered (dual and solo).
questions.explanation: The pre-stall checklist Altitude item states: Full Stall recovered before Dual 2000 ft AGL, Solo 3000 ft AGL.

questions.prompt: State the minimum altitudes by which an APPROACH to the stall must be recovered (dual and solo).
questions.explanation: The pre-stall checklist Altitude item states: Approach to the Stall recovered before Dual 1500 ft AGL, Solo 2500 ft AGL.

questions.prompt: Recite the complete pre-stall checklist: all four inside inspection items (with their required states) and all four outside inspection items.
questions.model_answer: Inside inspection: 1. Trim - Checked (trimmed for level flight); 2. Flaps - Retracted (UP); 3. Engine - Checked (instruments in green, fuel balanced); 4. Security - Checked (harnesses tight, baggage stowed). Outside inspection: 1. Altitude - Checked; 2. Position - Checked; 3. Orientation - Checked; 4. Sky - Free.
questions.explanation: The QRC pre-stall checklist lists these four inside items (Trim, Flaps, Engine, Security) and four outside items (Altitude, Position, Orientation, Sky), to be performed before every stall and every approach to the stall.

questions.prompt: The Position item of the pre-stall checklist says you must never stall above which of the following?
questions.explanation: The QRC Position item lists: never stall above built up areas, harbours and industrial areas, populated areas, airports/CTRs, extended water areas, 4/8 clouds or more, and other traffic. '4/8 clouds or more' is the only option on that list.

questions.prompt: For the Sky item of the pre-stall checklist, which clearing turns does the QRC prescribe to check the airspace ahead and below for other traffic?
choices: Two 180-degree turns, one in each direction
A single 360-degree turn to the left
90-degree right and left clearing turns, or a left-hand 180-degree turn
questions.explanation: The QRC Sky item states: make 90-degree right and left clearing turns or a left-hand 180-degree turn to check the airspace ahead and below for other traffic.

questions.prompt: Put the full stall recovery WITH power (clean) in the correct order.
steps: Pitch down to reduce the angle of attack, simultaneously call "RECOVER"
Check for increasing speed (about 70 KIAS)
Pitch up gently while moving the power lever gently forward to reach full power when the nose is passing through the horizon
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)
Climb back to original altitude
questions.explanation: This is the QRC 'Full stall recovery with power (clean)' sequence: reduce AoA and call RECOVER, confirm speed increasing (about 70 KIAS), full power as the nose passes the horizon, stay coordinated, pitch for 80 KIAS climb and regain the original altitude.

questions.prompt: Recovery from the approach to stall in the LANDING configuration is started at:
choices: Full back pressure with an excessive rate of descent
The nose or wing dropping through the horizon
5 KIAS below the bottom of the white arc
Stall warning, buffet, or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first
questions.explanation: The QRC states for approach to stall in the landing configuration: recover at the stall warning, buffet or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first. Nose/wing drop with full back pressure is the full-stall criterion.

questions.prompt: In the approach to stall in the landing configuration, below which speeds are the flap selections made (after calling "SPEED CHECKED")?
questions.explanation: The QRC approach-to-stall (landing configuration) procedure: check speed below 108 KIAS, call "SPEED CHECKED" and select flaps take-off; check speed below 91 KIAS, call "SPEED CHECKED" and select flaps landing.

questions.prompt: During the recovery from an approach to stall in the landing configuration, when are the flaps retracted fully up?
choices: Immediately with the application of full power
When the speed is above 70 KIAS, after selecting flaps take-off
When the speed is above 91 KIAS
Only after reaching the original altitude
questions.explanation: The QRC recovery sequence: full power, pitch for climb attitude, select flaps take-off, then at speed >70 KIAS select flaps up, then climb back to the previous altitude.

questions.prompt: Which bank angles does the QRC prescribe for the approach-to-stall manoeuvres in turns?
choices: Descending turn in approach configuration: 20 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 15 degrees
Descending turn in approach configuration: 30 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 20 degrees
Descending turn in approach configuration: 15 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 20 degrees
Descending turn in approach configuration: 45 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 30 degrees
questions.explanation: The QRC states: start the descending turn in approach configuration with 20 degrees of bank, and start the climbing turn with flaps retracted with 15 degrees of bank. 30 degrees is the normal/descending cruise-turn bank and 45 degrees is the steep-turn bank used elsewhere in the QRC.

questions.prompt: In the full stall recovery WITHOUT power (clean), after the pitch-down and "RECOVER" call with speed increasing through about 70 KIAS, you adjust pitch for:
choices: Glide attitude at 75 KIAS, and trim
questions.explanation: The QRC full stall recovery without power: pitch down, call "RECOVER", check increasing speed (about 70 KIAS), maintain coordination, then adjust pitch for glide attitude (75 KIAS) and trim; when established in the glide, end the exercise and climb back to the original altitude.

questions.prompt: What are the FIRST actions of the wing dip recovery in the QRC?
choices: Apply full opposite rudder, then pitch down
Apply full power and roll wings level with ailerons
Pull up gently while applying full power
questions.explanation: Wing dip recovery step 1 in the QRC is: power idle, ailerons neutral. Full opposite rudder comes only after the "Recover" call with pitch down below the glide attitude to break the stall.

questions.prompt: Put the wing dip recovery in the correct order.
steps: Power idle, ailerons neutral
Call "Recover" and simultaneously pitch down below the glide attitude to break the stall
Apply full opposite rudder with the feet
Neutralize the rudder with the feet when rotation stops
Check for increasing speed (about 80 KIAS)
Pull gently out of the dive, moving the power lever gently forward to reach full power when the nose passes through the horizon
Direction with the feet, no bank; adjust pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS) and climb back to the previous altitude
questions.explanation: This follows the QRC wing dip recovery: idle power and neutral ailerons first, break the stall with pitch down below glide attitude while calling "Recover", stop rotation with full opposite rudder, neutralize rudder when rotation stops, confirm about 80 KIAS, then recover from the dive reaching full power at the horizon and climb at 80 KIAS.

questions.prompt: During the wing dip recovery, at about what speed do you check for increasing speed before pulling out of the dive?
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery step 5 is: check for increasing speed (about 80 KIAS). 70 KIAS is the speed check in the full stall recovery; 75 KIAS is the glide speed.

questions.prompt: Put the QRC emergency (spin) recovery procedure - 'just in case you don't know the procedure anymore' - in the correct order.
steps: Power idle
Ailerons and elevator neutral
Apply full opposite rudder against the rotation
Neutralize the rudder
Pull gently out of the dive, wings level
Full power when the nose is passing the horizon
Climb back to the desired altitude
questions.explanation: This is the verbatim QRC emergency recovery sequence: power idle, ailerons and elevator neutral, full opposite rudder against rotation, neutralize rudder, pull gently out of the dive with wings level, full power at the horizon, climb back to the desired altitude.

questions.prompt: The QRC general emergency recovery procedure is stated to be applicable for:
choices: All aircraft, regardless of certification or loading
All JAR23 & FAR23 approved aircraft, provided mass & balance falls in the envelope and the aircraft is trimmed for cruise flight
Only the Diamond DA40-TDI, in any loading condition
All JAR23 & FAR23 approved aircraft, provided the aircraft is trimmed for approach
questions.explanation: The QRC states the general procedure is applicable for all JAR23 & FAR23 approved aircraft, provided mass & balance falls in the envelope and the aircraft is trimmed for cruise flight, and directs the pilot to consult the AFM/Diamond for the DA40 specific procedure.

questions.prompt: In the wing dip recovery, when do you neutralize the rudder?
choices: As soon as full opposite rudder is applied
When the nose passes through the horizon
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery: apply full opposite rudder with the feet, then neutralize the rudder with the feet when rotation stops.

questions.prompt: With the "Recover" call in the wing dip recovery, you simultaneously pitch down:
choices: To the horizon, then hold level
Below the glide attitude, to break the stall
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery step 2: call "Recover" and simultaneously pitch down below the glide attitude to break the stall.

questions.prompt: After the rotation has stopped in the wing dip recovery, how is direction controlled while pulling out of the dive?
choices: With ailerons, rolling into a 20-degree bank
With ailerons only, keeping the ball centered
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery states: direction with feet, no bank, then adjust pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS) and climb back to the previous altitude.

questions.prompt: What is the correct first call and first action for a rejected take-off?
choices: Make the RT call first, then close the power
Call "Aborting!" and close the power immediately
questions.explanation: The QRC rejected take-off: step 1 call out "Aborting!", step 2 close the power immediately, then maintain the centreline with rudder, brake as necessary, elevator neutral/aileron into the wind, RT call, and vacate the runway as soon as practical.

questions.prompt: Put the rejected take-off procedure in the correct order.
steps: Call out: "Aborting!"
Close the power immediately
Maintain runway centreline using the rudder
Apply brakes as necessary
Elevator neutral / aileron into the wind
RT call: "call sign, rejected take-off"
Vacate the runway as soon as practical
questions.explanation: This is the verbatim QRC rejected take-off sequence, from the "Aborting!" call and immediate power closure through braking, the rejected take-off RT call, and vacating the runway.

questions.prompt: Put the simulated engine failure after take-off (SEFATO) procedure in the correct order.
steps: Pitch for the glide attitude
Select a landing area and avoid obstacles
Troubleshoot (time permitting)
Select flaps take-off when the landing is assured
Adjust attitude for 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps)
Plan a full flaps landing
Crash drill
Touchdown
questions.explanation: This is the QRC SEFATO sequence: glide attitude, landing area selection, troubleshooting time permitting, flaps T/O when landing is assured, 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps), full flaps landing planned, crash drill, touchdown. For an actual failure: evacuate and call RAC; for training: go-around at minimum safe height.

questions.prompt: In the SEFATO procedure, which approach speeds does the QRC prescribe?
questions.explanation: The QRC SEFATO step: adjust attitude for 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps).

questions.prompt: For the glide-in from circuit altitude, how does the QRC modify the downwind leg?
choices: No flaps on downwind, speed 75 KIAS
No flaps on downwind, speed 90 KIAS
questions.explanation: The QRC glide-in procedure: fly the standard circuit but with no flaps on downwind at 90 KIAS, maintain circuit altitude on downwind/base depending on wind, close the power lever when the landing is assured, then glide at 75 KIAS.

questions.prompt: In the glide-in from circuit altitude, the QRC has you plan a full flaps landing with touchdown at:
questions.explanation: The QRC glide-in procedure: glide speed 75 KIAS, select flaps when the landing is assured, plan a full flaps landing and touch down at 60 KIAS. 65 KIAS is the short field landing approach speed and 70 KIAS the normal final speed.

questions.prompt: State the QRC flapless landing speeds on each circuit leg.
questions.explanation: The QRC flapless landing: maintain 90 KIAS on downwind, 85 KIAS on base leg, power/attitude 75 KIAS on final, with a nose attitude higher than for a normal landing and no flare-out at touchdown.

questions.prompt: Which technique does the QRC prescribe for the touchdown phase of a flapless landing?
choices: Do not flare out; maintain a slightly higher nose attitude during touchdown
Normal flare to a full-stall touchdown on the main wheels
Hold the aircraft off as long as possible at 60 KIAS
Close the power only after touchdown, in the tempo of the flare
questions.explanation: The QRC flapless landing states: nose attitude higher than for a normal landing, and do not flare out - maintain a slightly higher attitude during touchdown. Closing power in the tempo of the flare belongs to the short field landing.

questions.prompt: How does the QRC define a wave-off, and what does it say about the wheels?
choices: A go-around below 100 ft AGL; the wheels must never touch the runway
A go-around below 50 ft AGL; due to aircraft inertia the main wheels may briefly touch the runway - do not pull back excessively to prevent this, and do not deliberately land
A go-around below 50 ft AGL; if the wheels touch, you are committed to land
A rejected landing at any height; a brief touchdown always ends the manoeuvre
questions.explanation: The QRC wave-off: it is a go-around below 50 ft AGL; don't attempt turns at low altitude; due to inertia the main wheels may briefly touch the runway - do not pull back excessively to prevent this and do not deliberately land; then proceed as a go-around.

questions.prompt: Recite the crash drill items exactly as used in the SEFATO / forced landing context, including which items are touch-drill only.
questions.model_answer: Crash drill: Seat belts - fastened; Fuel selector - closed (T); Flaps - set; Electric Master - off (T). (T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY.
questions.explanation: The QRC crash drills list: seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps set, electric master off (T), where (T) means touch drill only. The crash drill is step 8 of the SEFATO procedure in the circuit emergencies exercise.

questions.prompt: Normal take-off: what is the FIRST call-out, made after confirming the correct runway from signage/markings?
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Normal take-off item 1: confirm correct runway from signage/markings and call “Runway [number], identified”. The other calls come later in the sequence.

questions.prompt: Which option lists only correct line-up items per the QRC?
choices: Parking brakes released; transponder ALT; landing light on when clearance received; pitot heat ON in visible moisture or OAT below +5°C
Parking brakes set; transponder ALT; landing light on when clearance received; pitot heat ON below +15°C
Parking brakes released; transponder 7700; landing light off for take-off; pitot heat ON in visible moisture or OAT below +5°C
Parking brakes released; transponder ALT; landing light on only after rotation; pitot heat ON below +10°C
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, line-up items: parking brakes released; transponder ALT; landing light on when clearance received; pitot heat ON in visible moisture or if OAT is below +5°C.

questions.prompt: Per the line-up items, when must the pitot heat be switched ON?
choices: In visible moisture or if OAT is below +5°C
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, line-up items: “Pitot heat ON (in visible moisture or if OAT is below +5°C)”.

questions.prompt: What does the CED check consist of during the take-off roll, before calling “Take-off power set”?
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Normal take-off item 10: “Check CED — power 100% / 2300 RPM / all indications green”, call out “Take-off power set”.

questions.prompt: Normal take-off (DA40-TDI): give the QRC values for rotation, initial climb, flap retraction height and final climb speed.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Normal take-off items 13, 14, 17, 18: rotate at 60 KIAS (Vr), climb 70 KIAS, flaps up passing 200 ft AGL, then climb 80 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Crosswind take-off in a strong crosswind (1/2 gust): what rotation speed does the QRC prescribe?
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Crosswind take-off item 2: “Vr + max 5 KIAS during strong crosswind (1/2 gust)”.

questions.prompt: Order the key steps of the short field take-off.
steps: Line up at the very beginning of the runway (use all available length)
Hold the brakes and set full power (100%) 2300 RPM
Check power / engine instruments
Release brakes, heels on the floor
Rotate at 55 KIAS (Vr)
Accelerate in ground effect once airborne
Start climb when speed > 59 KIAS
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Short field take-off: line up at the very beginning, hold brakes, full power 100%/2300 RPM, check instruments, release brakes, rotate 55 KIAS, accelerate in ground effect, climb when >59 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Soft field take-off: when do you release the back pressure on the stabilator?
choices: When the nose wheel lifts off
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Soft field take-off: make a rolling take-off, maintain back pressure on the stabilator, and “release back pressure when nose wheel lifts off”.

questions.prompt: Obstacle take-off: what is the initial climb speed, and what speed is flown after passing the obstacle?
choices: 55 KIAS initial, 70 KIAS after the obstacle
60 KIAS initial, 70 KIAS after the obstacle
70 KIAS initial, 80 KIAS after the obstacle
59 KIAS initial, 80 KIAS after the obstacle
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Obstacle take-off: “Initial climb 59 KIAS; speed 80 KIAS after passing obstacle”.

questions.prompt: In the normal circuit, what speed and power setting are used after levelling off at circuit altitude?
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit item 2: “Speed 90 KIAS, power ±45%”. (110/65% is cruise, 80/15% relates to base, 75 is glide.)

questions.prompt: Which bank limits apply in the normal circuit per the QRC?
choices: 20° for all turns in the circuit
30° bank for the crosswind and downwind turns; climbing turn after passing 200 ft max 20° bank; turn to final max 30° bank
45° bank for crosswind/downwind turns; 30° bank on final
30° bank for crosswind/downwind turns; climbing turn max 30°; final turn max 45°
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit: turns to crosswind and downwind use 30° bank (items 3, 5); a climbing turn after passing 200 ft is permitted with max 20° bank (item 4); turn to final uses maximum 30° of bank (item 11). (45° bank is the steep turn in Exercise 15.)

questions.prompt: Recite the FRESBL downwind checks from memory, with the content of each item.
questions.model_answer: F — Flaps: check speed, call “SPEED CHECKED” → select flaps take-off. R — Radio: downwind call (e.g., PH-RAB downwind runway 06). E — Engine: instruments in green, fuel quantity & balance checked. S — Security: harnesses secure, loose items stowed. B — Brakes: check pressure, heels on floor. L — Lights: landing light ON.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit item 6 lists the FRESBL downwind checks exactly as in the model answer.

questions.prompt: Normal circuit, base to final: give the QRC power setting on base, the descent speed, and the final approach speed with flaps LDG.

parts.label: Maintain altitude until, then descend at

questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit items 8, 9, 12: reduce power to ±15% on base, maintain altitude until 80 KIAS then start descent, on final flaps LDG and 70 KIAS trimmed.

questions.prompt: Order the normal circuit flow from downwind to established final.
steps: Perform the downwind checks (FRESBL)
Turn to base leg when the runway is 45° behind
Reduce power to ±15%
Maintain altitude until 80 KIAS, then start the descent
Turn to final with maximum 30° of bank
On final: flaps LDG, 70 KIAS, trimmed
Establish on a stabilized glide path
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit items 6–13 in this order.

questions.prompt: Order the go-around steps.
steps: Call: “Going-around!”
Set full power (100%)
Pitch up to arrest the descent (look outside)
Set flaps take-off
Pitch for climb attitude (70 KIAS)
Maintain coordinated flight and reset trim
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Go-around items 1–7: call “Going-around!”, full power 100%, pitch up to arrest descent, flaps T/O, climb at 70 KIAS, stay coordinated, reset trim.

questions.prompt: Crosswind landing: how is the aircraft aligned with the centreline just before touchdown?
choices: Keep the crab angle through touchdown
Bank away from the wind and use aileron to align
Use rudder to de-crab and line up, while banking into the wind
Touch down on the nose wheel first, then align
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Crosswind landing items 4–5: use rudder to de-crab and line up with the centreline, at the same time bank into the wind to stay above the centreline; land on the main wheels.

questions.prompt: Short field landing: what is the approach speed, and how is the power closed?
choices: 65 KIAS; close the power lever gently in the tempo of the flare, ideally just closed at touchdown
70 KIAS; close the power fully abeam the threshold
75 KIAS; keep power on until after touchdown
60 KIAS; close the power at the start of final
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Short field landing: power/attitude 65 KIAS, close the power lever gently in the tempo of the flare; ideally power should just be closed as the aircraft touches down (not before!).

questions.prompt: Touch and go: after aiming for the centreline, what is the correct sequence of configuration and power?
choices: Set flaps take-off (visual check), full power 100%/2300 RPM
Keep flaps landing, full power 100%/2300 RPM
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Touch and go: aim for the centreline, set flaps take-off (visual check), full power 100%/2300 RPM, proceed as normal take-off.

questions.prompt: Normal landing: which description matches the QRC?
choices: Aim for the aiming point, keep ±15% power through touchdown, touch down on the nose wheel first, do the after landing checks on downwind
Close the power at the start of final, hold 75 KIAS to touchdown, touch down on all wheels at once, do the after landing checks before vacating
Aim for the aiming point, close the power lever gently, flare, touch down on the main wheels, and perform the after landing checks after passing the stop bar
Aim at 1/3 of the runway, keep 70 KIAS to the flare, touch down tail-low on grass only, do the after landing checks on the runway
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal landing: aim for the aiming point, close the power lever gently, flare (item 10), touchdown on main wheels (item 11); after landing checks are memory items performed after passing the stop bar (item 16). (75 KIAS is the glide speed; aiming at 1/3 of the field belongs to the forced landing, Exercise 16.)

questions.prompt: Steep turn entry: what speed and bank angle does the QRC prescribe?
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn: speed 110 KIAS, roll into 45° bank using rudder to counteract adverse yaw.

questions.prompt: During the steep turn, how is power managed?
choices: Increase power by ±10% passing 30° bank; reduce power by ±10% when passing 30° bank on roll-out
Full power at 45° bank; idle on roll-out
Reduce power by ±20% passing 30° bank; increase on roll-out
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn items 4 and 7: passing 30° bank increase power by ±10%; when passing 30° of bank on roll-out, reduce power by ±10%.

questions.prompt: Steep turn: give the QRC entry speed, bank angle, and the bank angle at which the power change is made.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn: 110 KIAS, 45° bank, power ±10% passing 30° bank (both rolling in and rolling out).

questions.prompt: Order the steep turn steps.
steps: Look out – scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Set speed 110 KIAS
Roll into 45° bank, using rudder to counteract adverse yaw
Passing 30° bank, increase power by ±10%
Check bank/slip indicator, altitude/pitch, and maintain 110 KIAS
Roll out using rudder; passing 30° bank reduce power by ±10%
Adjust pitch for horizontal flight
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn items 1–8 in this order.

questions.prompt: Order the spiral dive recovery steps.
steps: Reduce the power
Roll out gently, wings level
Pitch up gently to climb attitude
Apply full power when the nose passes the horizon
Climb back to desired altitude
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Spiral dive recovery: reduce power first, then roll wings level, then pitch up gently — power and pitch only after the wings are level to avoid tightening the spiral.

questions.prompt: Spiral dive recovery: what is the FIRST action?
choices: Pull up firmly to stop the descent
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Spiral dive recovery item 1: “Reduce the power”, then roll out gently wings level, then pitch up gently. (Full opposite rudder belongs to wing dip/spin recovery in Exercise 11.)

questions.prompt: Forced landing: what is the first speed-related action after the engine failure?
choices: Pitch for 90 KIAS and start the Mayday call
Immediately select flaps T/O and slow to 60 KIAS
Maintain altitude till speed bleeds off to 75 KIAS, then pitch for glide attitude and trim for 75 KIAS
Dive to 110 KIAS to reach a distant field
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing items 1–2: maintain altitude till speed bleeds off to 75 KIAS while looking for a field, then pitch for glide attitude and trim for 75 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Forced landing: below which altitude do you turn direct to base leg for the most suitable landing area?
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing item 3: depending on altitude/position turn downwind; below 1200 ft turn direct base leg for the most suitable landing area.

questions.prompt: Forced landing: which emergency communication actions does the QRC list (time permitting)?
choices: PAN PAN call / transponder 7600 / ELT auto
Mayday call / transponder 7500 / landing light on
No radio call; all attention on flying only
Mayday call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T)
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing item 6: “May Day call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T) (when time permitting)”. (PAN PAN is used for the precautionary landing in Exercise 17.)

questions.prompt: On final in a forced landing, where should you initially aim in the field?
choices: At the very beginning of the field
At the last third of the field
At 1/3 of the field, to guarantee making the field
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing item 10: “On final aim at 1/3 of the field to guarantee making the field”; only when landing is assured shift the aiming point to the beginning of the field (item 14).

questions.prompt: Forced landing speeds: give the QRC values for the glide, the approach with flaps T/O, and the planned full-flaps landing speed.

parts.label: Flaps T/O when landing assured, adjust attitude for

questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing items 2, 11–13: trim 75 KIAS; flaps T/O when landing assured and adjust attitude for 70 KIAS; plan full flaps landing 60 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Order the forced landing procedure from engine failure to final approach.
steps: Maintain altitude till speed bleeds off to 75 KIAS; pitch for glide attitude and trim for 75 KIAS
Turn downwind and select a landing area (below 1200 ft turn direct base leg)
Perform abbreviated troubleshoot; Mayday call / transponder 7700 / ELT Man. (T)
Proceed to the 1000 ft point; expanded troubleshoot / restart if possible
After passing the 1000 ft point, turn to base leg
On final aim at 1/3 of the field; flaps T/O when landing assured
Adjust attitude for 70 KIAS; plan full flaps landing at 60 KIAS
Perform crash drills
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing procedure items 1–13 and crash drills, in QRC order.

questions.prompt: Forced landing crash drills: which set is correct, and what does (T) mean?
choices: Seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps set, electric master off (T); (T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY
Seat belts fastened, fuel selector open, flaps up, electric master on; (T) = TRAINING ONLY
Seat belts loose, fuel selector closed, flaps set, electric master off; (T) = TAXI ONLY
Seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps up, electric master on (T); (T) = TOUCHDOWN ONLY
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Crash drills: seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps set, electric master off (T); “(T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY!!!”.

questions.prompt: When should you consider a precautionary landing, and what are the QRC requirements for a landing field?
questions.model_answer: Consider a precautionary landing when: weather deteriorates below VMC minima; after UDP; or other circumstances affecting flight safety that require it (the aircraft should be technically in good condition). Field requirements: no obstacles on final (or upwind); long enough (minimum 300 m); headwind (or light crosswind); flat; preference for (short) grassland over plowed land.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, “Consider a precautionary landing when” and “Requirements for a landing field” lists.

questions.prompt: Precautionary landing: which radio/transponder/ELT actions does the QRC prescribe?
choices: PAN PAN call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T)
PAN PAN call / transponder 7600 / ELT off
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, procedure item 3: “PAN PAN call / transponder on 7700 / ELT man (T)”. (Mayday belongs to the forced landing, Exercise 16.)

questions.prompt: Precautionary landing: give the QRC circuit height, inspection run height, and minimum field length.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17: fly a close circuit at 500 ft AGL (item 5), inspection run at 200 ft AGL (item 7), field long enough min. 300 m (field requirements).

questions.prompt: In the precautionary landing pattern, when do you turn to final?
choices: When the landing area is 45° behind
When the landing area is 90° abeam
When the landing area is 60° behind the wing
Immediately after the inspection run at 200 ft AGL
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, procedure item 14: “Turn to final when the landing area is 60° behind the wing”. (45° behind is the base-turn cue in the normal circuit, Exercise 13.)

questions.prompt: Order the precautionary landing procedure after selecting the field.
steps: Perform downwind checks, select flaps T/O, PAN PAN call / transponder 7700 / ELT man (T)
Position on downwind of the suitable field and fly a close circuit at 500 ft AGL
Make a descending turn towards the area and carry out an inspection run at 200 ft AGL
Climb back to 500 ft AGL, flaps up on the up-wind leg, turn crosswind then downwind (downwind checks)
Turn to final when the landing area is 60° behind the wing
Carry out a short field landing
Evacuate the airplane and call RAC
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, Precautionary landing procedure items 1–16 condensed in QRC order.

questions.prompt: Soft field landing (grass runway): what does the QRC prescribe after touchdown?
choices: Brake firmly and bring the aircraft to a stop as soon as possible
Lower the nose immediately and vacate the runway at the first exit
Maintain backpressure on the elevator to relieve the nose wheel, decelerate gently without excessive brakes, keep the aircraft rolling, and perform the after landing checks while rolling
Hold the nose wheel off as long as possible, then stop on the runway to perform the after landing checks
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Soft field landing: after touchdown and during taxi maintain backpressure on the elevator to relieve the nose wheel, decelerate gently without excessive brakes, keep aileron in the wind, keep the aircraft rolling, and perform the after landing checks while rolling.
